PCI.BIO:
Professor of Electrical Engineering, Director and Founder of the US Dept. of Energy Industrial Assessment Center, Principal, Manufacturing Innovations Hub, and former founding Dean of the College of Engineering and Computer Science at UTRGV; James Clerk Maxwell Professor of Electrical Engineering and Director and Founder, Power Center for Utility Explorations, AAU R1 SUNY Buffalo; Professor of Electrical Engineering and Director, Power Center for Utility Explorations, R1 University of South Florida; Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering and Director, Florida Power Affiliates, AAU R1 University of Florida.

Significant efforts have included Demand Response Opportunity Pilots, Sustainable Electric Energy Delivery Systems (utility scale energy storage), Smart Energy pilots, Distributed Premium Power Park, Peak Load Shaving Technology with Renewable Resources (honored with the peak load management award), Advanced Commercial Energy technology for price response load management; developed a manufacturing innovations hub, established a US Dept of Energy Industrial Assessment Center, and a Weather and Reliability effort monitoring millions of utility customers, a Community Engagement Strategy to revitalize urban areas, and Gateway to Power $12M smart energy effort, certifications, dual degrees and international cooperative agreements.

MEDCONT.DESC:
IAC Program History
Industrial Assessment Centers (formerly called the Energy Analysis and Diagnostic Centers) were created by the Department of Commerce in 1976 in response to the oil embargo and rising energy costs. The program was specifically focused on helping small and medium-sized manufacturing facilities cut back on unnecessary costs from inefficient energy use.

The IAC program was moved to the Department of Energy just after it was formed in 1978 and was later expanded to include evaluations of ineffective production procedures, excess waste production, and other production-related problems. More recent additions to the IAC program scope include improving cybersecurity awareness, exploring smart manufacturing technologies, and implementing comprehensive energy management systems.

Currently the IAC program is administered through the Advanced Manufacturing Office under the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy at the Department of Energy.

SCHTEACH.TITLE: Advanced Energy Systems
SCHTEACH.PEDINN: This course will give students the ability to understand modern energy systems and analysis techniques used in research and in current wide-scale network energy and utility operations. Energy analysis of end-user facilities may be included. Discussions about energy systems worldwide including smart energy systems inclusive of distributed renewable sources will be addressed.
SCHTEACH.TECHMAT: Advanced energy systems will cover steady state operation of energy systems at the cutting edge of present development. Students will be introduced to fundamental principles and build up to advanced techniques so that they develop the basis to explore present and future energy systems as lifelong learners.
SCHTEACH.ENHSTUD: Students will be able to recognize and consider the operational aspects of energy components and systems on a local and wide-scale basis.  The intent is to begin to train the student in becoming an independent researcher and/or productive member of a company or academic team.  The course is taught by an interactive discourse between the instructor and student, and students with students.

CONGRANT.TITLE: South Texas Industrial Assessment Center
CONTENT_GOAL: GOAL 17: Partnerships to achieve the Goal
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
The US Department of Energy South Texas Industrial Assessment Center (ST-IAC) at UTRGV will provide assessments to small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to assist them with reducing costs in an extremely competitive environment. The assessments will focus on energy efficiency, productivity improvements, water management, cybersecurity, and sustainability, all supporting priorities to improve the resiliency of operations using renewables, decarbonization, and energy storage.

Over 90 students have been supported from all College departments thus far. Four faculty and two staff are funded. Cumulative funding exceeds +$3.2M at the present time. Of note is that the center is sustainably funded for most likely the next 40 years at increasing multi-million dollar levels of support. Furthermore, an industrial assessment lab was developed and funded.

The IAC is directly and uniquely written into the Infrastructure Law (there is no other center or initiative at UTRGV written into the infrastructure law). Legislation H.R. 3684 enacted in the summer of 2022 funded with $550M directly supporting the IAC efforts in Energy Efficiency. This recently enacted Act provides opportunities to reinforce the academic efforts of our UTRGV College of Engineering and Computer Science, by supporting the activities of the IAC.

In addition, all manufacturers now have the opportunity to apply for $400M (a max of $300K to each company) in support for implementations as developed by the Industrial Assessment Center team.

Note the IAC program name has been changed ​to the Industrial Training and Assessment Center (ITAC) effective 2025.

CONGRANT.TITLE: The Development of an Industrial Assessment Center for South Texas
CONGRANT.SPONORG: Department of Energy (DOE), Office of Energy Efficiency & Renewable Energy (EERE)
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
The four counties in deep south Texas known as the Rio Grande Valley are home to one of the fastest growing populations and one of the fastest growing manufacturing sectors in the state of Texas and world. The region is known as the Rio Grande Valley because it is located on the northern banks of the Rio Grande River which serves as the international boundary between the United States and Mexico. The Rio Grande Valley is also home to the second largest federally certified Hispanic Serving Institution (HSI) of higher education in the United States, the University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV). Approximately 90% of the more than 25,000 UTRGV students are Hispanic.
The UTRGV College of Engineering and Computer Science (CECS) has been recognized for the quality of its academic programs and the numerous partnerships and collaborations that its faculty have established with more than 100 entities in its service area including manufacturers, local governments, economic development councils, two year institutions of higher education and not-for-profit organizations. The undergraduate degrees that the CECS awards in civil engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, manufacturing / industrial engineering and computer science engineering are all accredited by the Accreditation Board for Engineering and Technology (ABET).
There is a tremendous need for the creation of the South Texas Industrial Assessment Center (South Texas IAC). In spite of the Rio Grande Valley’s rapidly growing population and the growing manufacturing sector the closest Industrial Assessment Center (IAC) to deep south Texas is 350 miles away. The development of the South Texas IAC will provide industrial energy assessments to small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) that previously did not have access to such no-cost energy assessments. Through the provision of these industrial energy assessments the South Texas IAC has the potential of assisting manufacturers to save millions of dollars each year in energy and water management costs.
The proposal to develop a South Texas Industrial Assessment Center (South Texas IAC) described herein is made possible because of a number of CECS engineering faculty who possess the requisite expertise and willingness to work with 20 UTRGV engineering students to carry out twenty industrial assessments per year. The faculty participating in the activities being proposed herein represent all of the departments in the CECS including electrical engineering, manufacturing and industrial engineering, civil engineering, and mechanical engineering. The diversity of faculty members’ areas of specialization and their various departmental affiliations in the CECS will provide students with an appreciation of the cross disciplinary nature of industrial energy assessments. The diversity of faculty will also ensure that engineering students throughout the CECS will become aware of the existence of the South Texas IAC and will have the opportunity to participate in the assessment activities as well as internships and research projects that come about as a result of the creation of the South Texas IAC.
As manufacturing enterprises in the Rio Grande Valley become aware of the tremendous financial benefits that accrue to them from the energy assessments offered through the South Texas IAC it is anticipated that small and large manufacturers alike will contribute to the financial viability of the South Texas IAC after grant funds expire.

INTELLCONT.TITLE_SECONDARY: ASME 2011 5th International Conference on Energy Sustainability, Parts A, B, and C
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: This paper shares initial results from a major collaborative project in Florida underway to study and address effects of high penetration levels of solar photovoltaic (PV) generation on the electric power system. The effort includes characterizing the variability of the solar resource in Florida, where a number of new multi-megawatt solar projects have either recently come online or are in the planning or construction stages (including the largest solar PV generating station in N. America at the time of this writing). Until now, most work on characterizing solar variability has focused on the Southwestern U.S. This paper shares initial results and insights on the variability of Solar PV generation output in Florida on different timescales and provides some preliminary insights into the implications and effects of the variability on the successful integration of increasingly higher penetration levels of solar PV, with respect to the integration technology, control systems, and the electric power system.
